Extend a series past its last observation

extend.Rd

Forecasts a single series: continues it from last to the end of the bank, in one of three ways. The series runs through anchor values (type = "level"); its growth rate runs through anchors, or follows a growth path, and the level is compounded (type = "growth"); or it continues with the growth or the changes of another series (type = "chain").

Usage

extend(
  x,
  ...,
  at = NULL,
  val = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  type = c("level", "growth", "chain"),
  growth = c("pca", "pcy"),
  method = c("ratio", "diff"),
  interp = c("linear", "stine"),
  last = NULL,
  hold_last = TRUE,
  smooth = NULL
)

Arguments

x

a ts-boxable object holding one series (quarterly, monthly or annual)

...

anchors as formulas, date on the left and value on the right: 2026.4 ~ 4.4, 2028.4 ~ 4.0. The right side is evaluated, so 2027.4 ~ target works. An alternative to at and val.

at

dates of the anchors, in any form to_ymd() reads (c(2026.4, 2028.4), c("2026Q4", "2028"))

val

anchor values (by name, like at): a numeric vector the length of at; a named numeric vector whose names are the dates (c("2026Q4" = 4.3)), with at = NULL; or a series (e.g. from make_xts()), whose observations are the anchors

path

instead of anchors, a series that sets the forecast: the level (type = "level"), the growth rate in percent (type = "growth"), or a level whose growth or changes continue x (type = "chain")

type

"level", "growth" or "chain" (see details)

growth

for type = "growth", how anchors and path state growth: "pca" (default), the period-on-period rate annualized (4.0 for a quarter that grew 1%); "pcy", the year-over-year rate

method

for type = "chain": "ratio" (default) continues x with the growth of path, for levels; "diff" with its changes, for rates (the same words as in chain())

interp

interpolation between anchors: "linear" or "stine" (the Stineman spline: smooth turns without overshooting)

last

last date that counts as history (default: the last observation of x). Values of x after last are replaced.

hold_last

if TRUE (default), the last anchor is held to the end of the bank. If FALSE, the interpolation itself runs to the last anchor and its value is then carried forward.

smooth

NULL, or a list with span and optionally from and to: smooth the forecast with loess before compounding (the period growth rate for "growth" and "chain", the level for "level"). from defaults to the first period after last.

Value

an object of the same type as x, from the bank start to the bank end (getOption("fcutils.bnk_start"), getOption("fcutils.bnk_end")), empty before x's first observation

Details

To join two sources of the same data, several series at once, or to extend a series back in time, use chain() instead. See "Which function" below.

  • type = "level": history up to last, then the anchors, with the gaps interpolated, including between the last history value and the first anchor. Anchors dated at or before last are dropped with a message, since history takes precedence.

  • type = "growth": the same applied to the growth rate of x; the level is then compounded from history. With growth = "pca" the line starts from the annualized growth at last and each period grows from the one before (annualized at the series' frequency: 4 for quarters, 12 for months). With growth = "pcy" it starts from the year-over-year growth at last, and each period grows from the same period a year earlier; this needs a full year of history and repeats last year's within-year pattern.

  • type = "chain": path after last, joined to x at last: scaled to meet it (method = "ratio") or shifted by a constant (method = "diff").

Linear interpolation weighs the gaps by time, the spline by position.

Which function. All of these continue a series from data:

  • levels at some dates: extend(type = "level");

  • growth rates at some dates, or a growth path, period-on-period or year-over-year: extend(type = "growth", growth = "pca"/"pcy");

  • another series' path (a projection, a model forecast), for one series: extend(type = "chain", method = "ratio"/"diff");

  • two sources of the same data to join, many series at once (each with its own method), or a series to extend back in time: chain().

extend() returns the series on the bank; chain() keeps the span of its inputs.

Anchors can be given in four ways: formulas (2026.4 ~ 4.4), at and val, a named vector (val = c("2026Q4" = 4.4)), or a series. Decimal dates such as 2026.4 are quarters, so a monthly series needs month strings ("2026M10" ~ 4.4); extend() stops if a monthly series gets decimal dates.

Examples

options(fcutils.bnk_start = as.Date("2015-01-01"), fcutils.bnk_end = as.Date("2035-12-31"))
ur <- make_xts(2024.1, val = c(3.8, 4.0, 4.2, 4.1, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3))
# the unemployment rate through two anchors, then held
extend(ur, 2026.4 ~ 4.4, 2028.4 ~ 4.0, interp = "stine")

# history continued with the growth of a projection on another level
proj <- make_xts(2020.1, val = 50 * 1.01^(0:63))
extend(cpi, path = proj, type = "chain")
